narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Windier and clearer than yesterday; temperatures little changed. Dry, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. 32°C / 90°F high, 19°C / 67°F low. Sky partly cloudy early as reported, mostly clear at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind NE early, SW at midday and WSW in the evening; gusts to 35 km/h (19 kt). UV index 9.5 (very high). Air quality 69 (moderate), by the CAMS model. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C / 73°F; low so far 20°C / 68°F; peak sustained 17 km/h; sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Next three days bring cooling through Saturday, with rain and thunderstorms likely each day. Thursday will be Mostly cloudy, Friday Mostly cloudy, Saturday Mostly cloudy. Thursday sees 4 of 4 models wet with rain 4.5–25.6 mm, high 31–32 °C, low 20 °C, gusts to 28 km/h (15 kt) and likely thunder. Friday is also 4 of 4 wet, rain 0.6–16.8 mm, high 28–31 °C, low 20 °C, gusts to 28 km/h (15 kt) and likely thunder. Saturday remains 4 of 4 wet, rain 2.8–56.6 mm, high 26–31 °C, low 19 °C, gusts to 25 km/h (14 kt) and likely thunder. The Day+3 high range is 26.5–30.9 °C, and Day+7 high range is 28.2–29.4 °C. Record line: Day+3 best rain record ECMWF, right 77% of the last 30 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Thunderstorm risk peaks this evening with CAPE values up to 3250 J/kg (UKMO) and a peak gust potential well above the forecast 35 km/h (19 kt). No formal warning has been issued by the Kenya Meteorological Department.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Over Winam Gulf the wind is east-northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 10 km/h (5 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 16 km/h (9 kt), and westerly into the evening at 12 km/h (7 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt). Peak gust reaches 25 km/h (14 kt). Thunderstorm gusts could exceed these values if storms develop.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1016 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the northeast, northwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1011.9 and 1014.1 hPa, near-steady over three days (-0.3 hPa). Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -0.7 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

Review notes that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, though Best Match slightly under-forecasts peak wind and ECMWF slightly over-forecasts overnight lows while under-forecasting daytime highs and peak wind. The call’s high of 32 °C matches the ECMWF under-forecast, while the peak gust of 35 km/h is slightly higher than Best Match’s estimate. The Kenya Meteorological Department provided no detailed bulletin, limiting direct comparison. Data sufficiency is good with 47 checks at Day+0, giving a settled picture despite uneven KMD coverage. Overall confidence is moderate, with model spread modest and most models agreeing on rain probabilities and thunder potential.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Monday. GFS is the wetter solution from Sunday to Monday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 29 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 56 checks.
